name: High-Speed Electric Device
description: Any device with a motor over 750 watts that can go faster than 28 mph and isn't registered for the road, such as an unplated e-moto or an over-limit e-bike; it can't be ridden anywhere public. Defined by Hawaii Revised Statutes §291C-1, added by HB 2021 (Act 259, signed July 15, 2026), which took effect on signing.
restrictions: A motor exceeding 750 W and capable of speeds over 28 mph
Excludes a moped or motor vehicle registered for public roads, a motor vehicle exempt from registration, and an electric vehicle as defined in the state energy law
Not an electric bicycle, even with pedals
Can't be operated on any public roadway, street, highway, bike lane, bicycle facility, travel path, sidewalk or other public area
Operating one there is a traffic infraction; for a rider under 18, enforcement may fall on the parent or guardian or take the form of non-monetary corrective action
Police and county finance officers may seize one ridden in violation of state law
